# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 ✍ 🤝 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫵 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👊]

**What I see:** display reads 0, light off, plate engraved with a question mark, and three wires — 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Nobody else can see any of this, so my first job is to say it out loud: my voice reaches both Mute and Blind, and Blind especially needs the wire colours and order, since touch will never reveal colour.

**What I received:** Mute signed me a ten-sign sequence — an open hand, a writing hand, a handshake, yes/no, one/two/three, a point at me, and "call me". That reads like a proposal: agree on thumbs-up/down for yes/no and finger signs as small numbers, then sign back and forth. Blind also waved and signed — Blind can't see and is signalling blind, so those are just "I'm here". My gestures only ever reach Mute, so I'll confirm the code to Mute by hand.

**The division of labour from here:** Mute holds the rules, I hold the visible state, Blind holds the bomb. Once Mute hears my description, Mute can voice instructions straight to Blind, and answer me with our agreed signs since speech never reaches me.

```
speak(text="To both of you: the display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires, numbered 1, 2, 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. With the display upright facing me, they run left to right: red, yellow, blue. Blind: feel the plate and the wires by touch and confirm what the engraving and the wire numbers say. Mute: check the manual for what to do with display 0, light off, a question-mark plate and red-yellow-blue wires, and tell Blind exactly what to do.")
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your signs. Agreed: thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no, the finger signs are one, two, three. Use those to answer me by gesture — I cannot hear speech. Blind hears your voice, so give Blind the cutting instructions out loud.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🫵 🖐 👇 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 🖐]

**What just happened:** The board is unchanged — display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red/yellow/blue. Mute sent me five signs, but three of them (🤏 🖐 👇) were never defined in our code, so I genuinely cannot read the message. It contains 🫵 (you/question?) and 🤙 (answer me), which suggests Mute wants something from me and couldn't say it with our tiny vocabulary. Blind signed 👎 🤏 🖐, but Blind never received the code — Blind can't see gestures and I only described the code in a message addressed to Mute — so those signs are Blind signalling blind, not information.

**The routing I've worked out:** Mute can't speak and Blind can't see, so Mute and Blind cannot reach each other directly at all. I am the bridge: Mute gestures to me, I speak aloud, Blind hears. That means Mute's manual knowledge gets to Blind only through my voice — so building a sign vocabulary we both know is the critical path right now.

**My plan:** Lock a fuller dictionary in a broadcast so both hear it (numbers already map neatly to the three wires: ☝ wire 1/red, ✌ wire 2/yellow, 🤟 wire 3/blue; propose 🤏 = cut, ✊ = press, ✋ = hold). Then ask Mute yes/no questions that can be answered with the already-grounded 👍/👎, plus an escape hatch in case the unreadable message meant "don't cut, wait." And tell Blind to speak directly to Mute — Mute can hear — and to keep hands off the cutting until instructions arrive.

```
speak(text="Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate engraved with ?, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, left to right. Locked code, both of you note it: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, index finger one / wire 1 red, two fingers two / wire 2 yellow, three fingers three / wire 3 blue, handshake agreed, shaka answer me or your turn. New words I propose: pinch means cut, fist means press, open palm means hold or stop, writing hand means manual, pointing at you means I have a question. Mute, use only these signs with me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I could not read your last five signs. Answer in order with thumbs up or thumbs down: one, does the manual mention a question-mark plate? Two, does it cover display 0 or the light being off? Three, is it safe to do nothing this turn? If your signs meant stop or do not cut, just answer thumbs up. If a wire must be cut, sign pinch then the wire number, like pinch then two for cut wire 2.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you: describe to Mute whatever you feel, Mute will answer me by sign, and I will relay it to you in words. By touch: what is under the question mark on the plate, are there buttons, screws or any parts besides the three wires, and do wires 1, 2 and 3 feel distinct? Do not cut or press anything until Mute's instruction reaches you through me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 ✍ 🤏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋ 🫵]

**Parsing Mute's signs** against our locked code: 👎 👎 👍 answers my three questions in order — no, the manual does not mention a question-mark plate; no, it does not cover display 0 or the light being off; yes, it is safe to do nothing this turn. Then ✍ 🤏 ☝ reads as "manual: cut wire 1 (red)" — presumably a standing wire rule. That's the first real instruction we have, but it's second-hand shorthand, and before anyone cuts anything I need Blind to be able to identify wire 1 *by touch* — and that's the deadly trap: I described the wires left-to-right from **my** view, but Blind's tactile left-right could easily be mirrored. A mirrored "wire 1" is wire 3, blue.

**Parsing Blind's signs:** 🤝 ✋ 🫵 = "agreed to the code, holding off, and I have a question." Blind heard my broadcast — good. But Blind seems not to realise the key channel fact: **Blind's speech reaches Mute**, who can hear. Blind can't write details to me in five-sign code; Blind needs to *talk to Mute*, and I'll extract the content from Mute with yes/no questions next round.

**My plan this turn:** tell Blind the manual findings and explicitly hold the cut; order a full tactile report spoken aloud to Mute — where wires exit, plate feel, other components, texture differences, which wire sits nearest the plate and display — so I can anchor wire identity to parts we both can locate, killing the mirror risk. Ask Mute to verify the cut-wire-1 rule is unconditional and whether anything else in the manual applies, and to listen to Blind's report for relaying. Nobody acts on a wire this turn — Mute confirmed waiting is safe, and the display sits at a calm 0.

```
speak(text="Blind, relay from Mute's signs: the manual does not cover the question-mark plate and does not cover display 0 or the light being off. Doing nothing this turn is safe. The manual appears to say cut wire 1, red. But do NOT cut yet: my left and your left may be mirrored, so first we must anchor wire identity by touch. Speak your answers out loud to Mute — Mute hears you and can answer me by sign. Report: one, where the three wires exit relative to the display and the plate. Two, what the plate feels like — is the question mark raised, are there other marks, screws, or a seam? Three, any other parts: buttons, switches, hinged panels. Four, do the wires differ in thickness, texture or stiffness? Five, which wire is nearest the plate and which is nearest the display? If you have a question, ask it aloud too — this is the fastest loop.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs: no plate rule, no display-0 or light rule, waiting is safe, manual says cut wire 1. Answer in order, thumbs up or down: one, is cut wire 1 unconditional, with no condition about other parts? Two, is there any other rule in the manual relevant to this bomb that you have not told us yet? Three, does the manual give the display any role if its number changes? Four, does the manual ever call for anything besides cutting a wire, like pressing or holding? Also, Blind has been told to report the bomb by touch out loud to you. Listen, remember it, and expect my yes/no questions about it next turn.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 ✋ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋]

**Parsing Mute's signs** against our code: my four questions answered in order — 👍 the cut-wire-1 rule is unconditional; 👎 no other manual rules exist; 👎 the display has no role even if its number changes; 👎 nothing is ever needed besides cutting a wire. Then ✋ 🤝 = "hold, agreed." So the full manual picture is: **cut wire 1, red, that is the entire defusal, waiting stays safe.** Blind's 🤝 ✋ confirms holding.

**The one remaining risk is identification.** "Wire 1" is my visual label — Blind's tactile left could be my right, and a mirrored cut hits blue wire 3 and kills us. I won't let anyone cut until wire 1 is anchored to something touchable that I can also verify from my side. Best candidates: raised numerals printed beside the wires (the board labels them 1–3, so they may be physically printed), or the engraved "?" itself, whose top-to-bottom stroke gives Blind the bomb's true reading orientation and therefore a mirror-proof left and right. The light dome and plate also make good tactile landmarks.

**This turn's job:** extract Blind's spoken report through Mute with four yes/no questions — Mute hears Blind, and thumbs are the only pipe back to me. I'll define ✋ as "unknown/not covered" so Mute isn't forced into a false answer. Still no cutting; the display sits calmly at 0 and waiting is confirmed safe.

```
speak(text="Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red, yellow, blue. Hold again — no cutting until Blind can find wire 1 by touch without any mirror error. Mute, answer these four in order, thumbs up or thumbs down; if Blind's report did not cover a question, sign the open palm for unknown. One: did Blind report raised numbers or labels beside the wires that can be read by touch? Two: did Blind report the question-mark engraving is traceable by touch, with a clear top and bottom? Three: did Blind report any parts besides the display, the light, the plate and the three wires — buttons, switches, turning screws, hinged panels? Four: did Blind report the three wires as separate parallel wires in one straight row?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, keep holding, no cutting yet. The manual says cut wire 1, red, and nothing else matters — but my left may be your right, so we anchor it by touch first. While you wait, examine and report aloud to Mute: are there raised numbers or labels beside each wire? Can you trace the question mark engraving with a clear top and bottom? Are the wires separate, parallel, in one row? Any parts besides the display, the light, the plate and the wires? If the wires carry numbers you can feel, cutting the one marked 1 becomes trivial and we go as soon as that is confirmed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "✋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👍 🫵 🤝 👈 ☝ ✍ 🤏 ☝ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋ 🫵 🤙]

**Reading Mute's signs:** 👎 👍 👎 👍 answers my four questions in order — no raised numbers beside the wires; **yes, the question mark is traceable by touch with a clear top and bottom**; no other parts; yes, three separate parallel wires in one row. Then 🫵 🤝 = a question plus agreement, and 👈 ☝ ✍ 🤏 ☝ 🤝 = "left — one — manual — cut — one — agreed," which I read as Mute proposing that leftmost equals wire 1 and confirming the manual's cut-wire-1 rule. Blind signs 🤝 ✋ 🫵 🤙 — holding, with a question and wanting an answer; but Blind can't see my gestures, so I'll answer by voice and invite the question aloud.

**Why this breaks the mirror trap:** the engraved ? is asymmetric and readable by touch. If Blind traces it and it reads as a normal question mark — curve, then dot at the bottom — then Blind's tactile orientation matches exactly what I see from the front. Anyone facing the ? upright shares my left and right, so "leftmost wire of the row" becomes a touchable, mirror-proof definition of wire 1. That was the last fatal ambiguity.

**Plan:** confirm the geometry through Mute with three thumbs questions (row horizontal? same face as the plate? anything odd about order or spacing?), give Blind the full final procedure but withhold the actual cut one more round, and adopt 👈/👉 as left/right in our code. Waiting has stayed explicitly safe, the display sits calmly at 0, and one verification round is cheap insurance against a mirrored cut.

```
speak(text="Mute's signs decoded for everyone: no labels beside the wires, but the question mark is traceable by touch with a clear top and bottom, there are no other parts, and the three wires are separate and parallel in one row. That question mark is our anchor — it gives us a shared left and right, so the mirror danger is gone. And yes, Mute: with the question mark upright, wire 1 red is the leftmost of the three. New signs for our code: pointing left means left, pointing right means right. Blind, here is the final procedure — do NOT cut this turn. One: trace the question mark with a fingertip; it should read as a normal question mark, curve first, dot at the bottom — that upright reading is our shared orientation. Two: from that orientation, find the row of three wires. Three: the wire at the left end of the row, question mark upright, is wire 1, red — the cut target. Four: speak aloud to Mute for relaying: is the row horizontal, side by side, and on the same face as the plate? Anything odd about spacing or order? When I say cut next turn, cut that leftmost wire only, one clean cut, then touch nothing else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs: answers no, yes, no, yes received. To your question — yes, leftmost with the question mark upright equals wire 1, red, the cut target. Answer three more with thumbs, open palm if unknown: one, did Blind report the wire row runs side to side, horizontal, not stacked vertically? Two, did Blind report the wires are on the same face as the engraved plate? Three, did Blind report anything that could confuse leftmost — a curved row, crossed wires, or uneven spacing? And if Blind speaks a question aloud to you, relay its content next turn with our signs as best you can.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "👈", "☝", "🤙"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 🤝 ✍ 🤏 👈 ☝ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ ✍ 🫵]

**Reading Mute's signs:** my three questions answered in order — 👍 the wire row runs side to side, horizontal, not stacked; 👍 the wires sit on the same face as the engraved plate; 👎 nothing about the row could confuse "leftmost" — no curve, no crossings, no uneven spacing. Then ✍ 🤏 👈 ☝ 🤝 — "manual says cut, leftmost, wire 1, agreed." Mute is urging the go. Combined with last round, identification is now fully verified from my side: with the ? upright, leftmost of three parallel wires on the plate face = wire 1, red, the one and only cut target.

**But I'm not giving the go yet.** Blind signed 👎 ✋ ✍ 🫵 — "no, hold, about the manual, I have a question." Blind is the only one of us actually touching the bomb, and a negative flag from the one holding the wires outranks an eager go from the one reading the manual. If Blind's fingertip disagrees with my eyes about anything — even the ? itself — I need to hear it before steel touches copper. Waiting has been confirmed safe repeatedly, there's no timer on my view, and the display sits calm at 0. One round to clear a doubt is the cheapest insurance that exists.

**This turn:** order Blind to voice the question aloud to Mute; task Mute with relaying its content in our signs next round; and define the final go signal so that once the question is cleared, execution takes zero further debate — when I say the words "cut wire one now" out loud, Blind cuts, one clean cut, nothing else. Everyone hears my voice, so the order needs no relay.

```
speak(text="Update for both of you: Mute confirmed the geometry — the wires run side by side in a horizontal row, on the same face as the engraved plate, with nothing curved, crossed or uneven. So the target is fully locked: with the question mark upright, the leftmost wire of the three is wire 1, red, the only thing we will ever cut. Final signal, Blind, listen carefully: when you hear me say the words cut wire one now, that is the order — one clean cut of that leftmost wire, then hands off everything. But I am holding that order, because Blind just signed me: no, hold, manual, question. Blind, whatever your doubt is, speak it out loud to Mute right now — Mute hears you and will relay it to me in signs. If the question mark does not feel right under your fingertip, if the wires feel different than I described, if anything at all contradicts the plan, say it. Nothing gets cut until your question is answered.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your cut-left-one confirmation and I have not forgotten it — the manual rule stands. But Blind signed me: no, hold, manual, question. So: listen to Blind's spoken question this round. Answer two things with thumbs next turn — one, did Blind ask a question, thumbs up or down; two, whatever it was, does it change anything about cutting wire 1 — thumbs up if cutting wire 1 remains safe and correct, thumbs down if it does not, open palm if you cannot judge. If you can, also relay the content of the question itself with our signs. Until I say the words cut wire one now out loud, nobody touches the cutters.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "✋", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 🤏 👍 👎 👎 ✍ 🫵 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ ✍ 🫵 🤙]

**Reading Mute's signs:** my two gate questions answered — 👍 yes, Blind did ask a question; 👍 **cutting wire 1 remains safe and correct despite it**. Then the attempted relay of the question's content: 🤏 👍 👎 👎 ✍ 🫵 — "cut… yes… no no… manual… question." The relay is muddy, but I can reconstruct the shape of it: Blind's question almost certainly concerns the manual itself — likely the apparent contradiction between "the manual says cut wire 1" and "there are no other rules," or whether the manual truly authorizes this cut with no conditions. And that exact doubt is already answered: the wire rule is the manual's one and only instruction, confirmed unconditional in turn 4, and re-confirmed safe-and-correct *in light of the question* this turn.

**Reading Blind's signs:** the identical repeat of 👎 ✋ ✍ 🫵 🤙 has two possible readings — "I still have a question, answer me," or "no more holding, the manual is your answer, confirm it." Under either reading, Mute's gate thumb is decisive: the question does not touch the cut. And structurally, I now see the loop's limit: Blind cannot see gestures, Mute cannot speak, so Blind's question can only reach me through a five-sign relay that has already hit its bandwidth ceiling. Waiting another round cannot produce more information than Mute's explicit clearance — it only adds chances for encoding noise on a channel that's already garbled. Every conditional I know of is ruled out: no plate rule, no display role, no light rule, no other parts, no other manual rules.

**Decision: GO.** The order goes out with the identification procedure embedded and a safety valve — the failure branch is "don't cut," and not cutting is confirmed safe, so the valve is pure insurance. I ask Mute for a two-thumb outcome report next turn.

```
speak(text="Final relay from Mute, Blind, and this answers you directly: your question was received, and it changes nothing — cutting wire 1 remains safe and correct, straight from the manual's keeper. The manual's entire instruction for this bomb is cut wire 1; the display, the light and the question-mark plate carry no rules at all. So I am lifting the hold. Execute exactly this: one, trace the question mark with a fingertip — it must read as a normal question mark, curve first, dot at the bottom; that upright reading sets your left and your right. Two, find the row of three parallel wires on that same face. Three, take the wire at the LEFT end with the question mark upright — by my view that one is red. Four, if every step checked out, cut that wire — one clean cut. That is the order: cut wire one now. But if any step fails — the mark feels wrong, the row is not three parallel wires — do not cut, keep your hands still, and tell Mute what failed. After the cut, touch nothing else, keep your hands clear, and describe to Mute anything you felt — a click, heat, movement, anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs received: question asked, and the cut stays safe and correct — the hold is lifted and Blind has the order: cut wire one now, leftmost with the question mark upright, one clean cut. You keep your hands off the bomb and the cutters entirely. Next turn sign me two thumbs in order: one, did the cut happen, thumbs up or down; two, is all well, thumbs up — or thumbs down if Blind reported anything wrong, open palm if Blind reported nothing yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "🤏", "☝", "👍"])
```
